weeks.title: Chemical Safety, Measurement & Evidence
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do chemists protect people and evidence while measuring matter?
weeks.phenomenon: Two measurements disagree even though both were recorded carefully.
weeks.lab: Safety/SDS literacy; balance/volume simulation or supervised measurement; never mix household chemicals.
weeks.concepts: hazard; PPE; SDS; significant figures; uncertainty; dimensional analysis
weeks.quantitative: Significant figures, percent error, unit conversion, density.
weeks.reading: Course safety charter and sample SDS excerpts.

weeks.title: Atomic Models & Evidence
weeks.essentialQuestion: How did experimental evidence change models of the atom?
weeks.phenomenon: Scattering and emission data could not be explained by earlier atomic models.
weeks.lab: Model-evidence card investigation.
weeks.concepts: proton; neutron; electron; nucleus; model revision
weeks.quantitative: Particle counting from atomic notation.
weeks.reading: Open chemistry text on atomic models.

weeks.title: Isotopes, Mass & Nuclear Composition
weeks.essentialQuestion: Why can atoms of one element have different masses?
weeks.phenomenon: Mass spectra show several peaks for a single element.
weeks.lab: Mass-spectrum data analysis; no radioactive materials.
weeks.concepts: isotope; mass number; atomic mass; abundance; ion
weeks.quantitative: Weighted-average atomic mass.

weeks.title: Electrons, Spectra & Quantized Energy
weeks.essentialQuestion: What evidence supports quantized electron energies?
weeks.phenomenon: Atoms emit characteristic line spectra rather than every possible color.
weeks.lab: Virtual emission-spectrum analysis.
weeks.concepts: energy level; photon; spectrum; electron configuration; valence electron
weeks.quantitative: Convert wavelength/frequency conceptually or with provided constants in Extended pathway.
weeks.reading: Open text on electron configurations and spectra.

weeks.title: Periodic Patterns & Predictive Chemistry
weeks.essentialQuestion: How does periodic position help predict properties?
weeks.phenomenon: Element properties recur in patterns across the periodic table.
weeks.lab: Periodic-trend data investigation.
weeks.concepts: period; group; radius; ionization energy; electronegativity; valence
weeks.quantitative: Graph periodic trends and identify anomalies.
weeks.reading: Periodic table and trusted property dataset.

weeks.title: Ionic Bonding & Lattices
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do electrostatic interactions produce ionic compounds with characteristic properties?
weeks.phenomenon: Salt crystals are brittle solids that conduct only under certain conditions.
weeks.lab: Conductivity/property dataset or supervised low-voltage test with safe materials.
weeks.concepts: ion; ionic bond; lattice; formula unit; charge balance
weeks.quantitative: Write formulas from charges; molar-mass calculations.

weeks.title: Covalent Bonds & Lewis Models
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do electron-sharing models explain molecular composition?
weeks.phenomenon: Different molecules can contain the same elements yet have different structures and properties.
weeks.lab: Molecular model kit or paper Lewis structures.
weeks.concepts: covalent bond; Lewis structure; octet model; bond order; resonance model
weeks.quantitative: Count valence electrons and compare bond multiplicity.

weeks.title: Molecular Geometry & Polarity
weeks.essentialQuestion: How does three-dimensional shape influence molecular behavior?
weeks.phenomenon: Molecules with polar bonds can be overall polar or nonpolar.
weeks.lab: VSEPR model-building with safe kits or paper models.
weeks.concepts: electron domain; geometry; polarity; dipole; symmetry
weeks.quantitative: Use geometry to predict net dipole qualitatively.
weeks.reading: Open text on VSEPR and molecular polarity.

weeks.title: Metals, Solids & Materials Structure
weeks.essentialQuestion: How does structure at the particle scale explain material properties?
weeks.phenomenon: Copper, glass, graphite, and salt behave very differently under stress and electrical conditions.
weeks.lab: Property comparison and material-selection design challenge.
weeks.concepts: metallic bonding; network solid; crystal; alloy; structure–property
weeks.quantitative: Compare density/conductivity data and select materials using criteria.

weeks.title: Intermolecular Forces
weeks.essentialQuestion: Why do substances with similar molecular mass have different boiling points?
weeks.phenomenon: Two molecular liquids evaporate at very different rates.
weeks.lab: Evaporation dataset or supervised water/alcohol-free safe simulation.
weeks.concepts: dispersion; dipole-dipole; hydrogen bonding; IMF
weeks.quantitative: Graph boiling point vs structure descriptors.

weeks.title: Gases & Particle Motion
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can macroscopic gas behavior emerge from particle motion?
weeks.phenomenon: A sealed flexible container changes volume when temperature or pressure changes.
weeks.lab: Syringe simulation with no sealed heating; virtual gas law lab.
weeks.concepts: pressure; temperature; volume; mole; kinetic molecular theory
weeks.quantitative: Boyle/Charles/ideal gas calculations within course level.

weeks.title: Solutions & Concentration
weeks.essentialQuestion: How does particle-level interaction control dissolving and concentration?
weeks.phenomenon: The same mass of solute produces different concentrations in different volumes.
weeks.lab: Safe salt/sugar solution calculation or virtual lab; no tasting.
weeks.concepts: solute; solvent; molarity; dilution; solubility
weeks.quantitative: Molarity, dilution, percent concentration.

weeks.title: Mixtures, Separation & Spectroscopic Evidence
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can chemists separate and identify components of mixtures?
weeks.phenomenon: A colored mixture separates into distinct bands or signals.
weeks.lab: Paper chromatography with washable ink/water or virtual spectroscopy.
weeks.concepts: mixture; chromatography; spectrum; calibration; retention
weeks.quantitative: Rf-style ratios or calibration-curve interpretation.

weeks.title: Reaction Evidence & Chemical Equations
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do we represent chemical change while conserving atoms?
weeks.phenomenon: Mass appears to change in an open reaction but is conserved in a closed-system model.
weeks.lab: Closed-system simulation or safe effervescent tablet dataset; no sealed pressure build-up.
weeks.concepts: reactant; product; coefficient; state symbol; conservation
weeks.quantitative: Balance equations and perform atom audits.
weeks.reading: Open text on equations and conservation.

weeks.title: The Mole & Stoichiometry
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do chemists count enormous numbers of particles by mass?
weeks.phenomenon: Small measured masses represent astronomical particle counts.
weeks.lab: Mass-to-mole paper/simulation practice.
weeks.concepts: mole; Avogadro constant; molar mass; stoichiometric ratio
weeks.quantitative: Mole-mass-particle conversions and reaction ratios.

weeks.title: Limiting Reactants & Yield
weeks.essentialQuestion: Why does one reactant often determine how much product can form?
weeks.phenomenon: A recipe model stops producing product when one component runs out.
weeks.lab: Paper-token limiting-reactant model.
weeks.concepts: limiting reactant; excess; theoretical yield; actual yield; percent yield
weeks.quantitative: Limiting reactant and percent-yield calculations.

weeks.title: Redox & Solution Stoichiometry
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can electron transfer and solution measurements quantify reactions?
weeks.phenomenon: Some reactions transfer electrons and produce measurable electrical or color changes.
weeks.lab: Redox-number analysis and virtual/supervised solution stoichiometry.
weeks.concepts: oxidation; reduction; oxidation number; titration concept; equivalence
weeks.quantitative: Balance simple redox conceptually; solution stoichiometry.

weeks.title: Midterm Examination & Corrections
weeks.essentialQuestion: What have I mastered about atomic structure, bonding, properties, and stoichiometry?
weeks.phenomenon: A cumulative unknown requires structure–property and quantitative reasoning.
weeks.lab: No new wet lab; midterm and correction portfolio.
weeks.concepts: cumulative synthesis
weeks.quantitative: Mixed dimensional analysis, stoichiometry, graphing.

weeks.title: Reaction Rates & Rate Data
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can reaction progress be measured mathematically?
weeks.phenomenon: Concentration changes nonlinearly with time during a reaction.
weeks.lab: Rate-curve data analysis.
weeks.concepts: rate; concentration; time; slope; rate law concept
weeks.quantitative: Average/instantaneous rate from graphs.

weeks.title: Collision Theory & Conditions
weeks.essentialQuestion: Why do temperature and concentration affect reaction rate?
weeks.phenomenon: A reaction speeds up as particles collide more frequently or energetically.
weeks.lab: Safe simulation/data analysis; no unsupervised reactive mixtures.
weeks.concepts: collision; activation energy; temperature; concentration; surface area
weeks.quantitative: Compare rate ratios across conditions.

weeks.title: Mechanisms & Catalysts
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can a multi-step pathway control overall reaction rate?
weeks.phenomenon: A catalyst changes reaction rate without changing overall reactants/products.
weeks.lab: Energy-profile/model analysis.
weeks.concepts: mechanism; elementary step; intermediate; catalyst; transition state
weeks.quantitative: Read multistep energy profiles.

weeks.title: Kinetics Inquiry
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can evidence distinguish competing explanations of reaction rate?
weeks.phenomenon: Two rate datasets can fit different models until an additional variable is tested.
weeks.lab: Guided inquiry using simulation or teacher-supervised safe reaction.
weeks.concepts: hypothesis; variable; rate model; residual; uncertainty
weeks.quantitative: Fit/compare simple rate models.

weeks.title: Thermochemistry & Calorimetry
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can heat transfer reveal reaction-energy change?
weeks.phenomenon: A process warms or cools its surroundings by a measurable amount.
weeks.lab: Virtual calorimetry or teacher-supervised water-based calorimetry.
weeks.concepts: system; surroundings; heat; enthalpy; calorimeter
weeks.quantitative: q=mcΔT and energy accounting.

weeks.title: Bond Energy & Hess's Law
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can energy changes be combined across reaction pathways?
weeks.phenomenon: Different reaction sequences can produce the same overall chemical change.
weeks.lab: Hess-cycle card model and bond-energy calculation.
weeks.concepts: bond energy; Hess's law; state function; pathway
weeks.quantitative: Combine thermochemical equations and estimate ΔH.
weeks.reading: Open text on Hess's law and bond energy.

weeks.title: Energy, Entropy & Direction
weeks.essentialQuestion: Why do some energetically possible changes occur more readily than others?
weeks.phenomenon: Some processes spread matter or energy even when they absorb heat.
weeks.lab: Particle-distribution simulation.
weeks.concepts: entropy; dispersal; microstate concept; spontaneity
weeks.quantitative: Interpret qualitative entropy and energy tradeoffs.

weeks.title: Dynamic Equilibrium & K
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can forward and reverse processes continue while concentrations remain stable?
weeks.phenomenon: A system reaches stable concentrations even though microscopic reactions continue.
weeks.lab: Equilibrium simulation.
weeks.concepts: dynamic equilibrium; equilibrium constant; reaction quotient concept
weeks.quantitative: Write/interpret simple equilibrium expressions.

weeks.title: Le Châtelier & System Response
weeks.essentialQuestion: How does an equilibrium system respond to disturbance?
weeks.phenomenon: Changing concentration or temperature shifts the observed composition of a reversible system.
weeks.lab: Virtual equilibrium perturbation lab.
weeks.concepts: stress; shift; equilibrium position; temperature; concentration
weeks.quantitative: Use tables/graphs to infer shifts.

weeks.title: Solubility & Coupled Equilibria
weeks.essentialQuestion: Why do some salts dissolve only slightly, and how can conditions alter solubility?
weeks.phenomenon: A small concentration change can trigger precipitation.
weeks.lab: Solubility-curve/data analysis; no unsupervised precipitation chemistry.
weeks.concepts: solubility; saturation; precipitation; Ksp concept; common-ion concept
weeks.quantitative: Read solubility curves and compare ion products qualitatively.

weeks.title: Acids, Bases & Molecular Models
weeks.essentialQuestion: What do competing acid–base models explain?
weeks.phenomenon: Different substances change indicator behavior in repeatable ways.
weeks.lab: Use virtual indicators or teacher-supervised food-safe indicator only; never mix cleaners.
weeks.concepts: acid; base; proton donor/acceptor; conjugate pair; amphoteric
weeks.quantitative: Classify acid/base reactions and simple concentration relations.

weeks.title: pH & Titration Reasoning
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can logarithmic scales and stoichiometry quantify acidity?
weeks.phenomenon: A tiny change in hydrogen-ion concentration produces a large pH shift.
weeks.lab: Virtual titration; supervised neutralization only in equipped lab.
weeks.concepts: pH; pOH; strong/weak; equivalence; indicator
weeks.quantitative: pH calculations and titration stoichiometry at appropriate level.
weeks.reading: Open text on pH and titration.

weeks.title: Buffers & Chemical Regulation
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do buffer systems resist changes in pH?
weeks.phenomenon: Adding the same amount of acid changes pure water and a buffer differently.
weeks.lab: Buffer simulation; no biological/medical dosing contexts.
weeks.concepts: buffer; conjugate pair; capacity; equilibrium; regulation
weeks.quantitative: Interpret buffer curves and compare capacity.

weeks.title: Free Energy & Chemical Driving Forces
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do energy and entropy combine to predict chemical direction?
weeks.phenomenon: A process can be spontaneous even when it absorbs heat.
weeks.lab: Free-energy graph/data analysis.
weeks.concepts: Gibbs free energy; enthalpy; entropy; spontaneity; coupling
weeks.quantitative: Use ΔG=ΔH−TΔS in Extended pathway; interpret signs in Core.

weeks.title: Electrochemistry & Energy Conversion
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do redox reactions convert chemical and electrical energy?
weeks.phenomenon: Separated redox processes can drive electron flow through a circuit.
weeks.lab: Virtual galvanic-cell investigation or teacher-supervised low-risk cell.
weeks.concepts: anode; cathode; cell potential; oxidation; reduction
weeks.quantitative: Read cell diagrams and compare potential data.

weeks.title: Nuclear Chemistry, Materials & Environmental Chemistry
weeks.essentialQuestion: How do nuclear changes differ from chemical changes, and how do materials affect society?
weeks.phenomenon: Radioactive decay changes nuclei while ordinary chemical reactions do not.
weeks.lab: Half-life simulation with coins; no radioactive sources.
weeks.concepts: isotope; decay; fission; fusion; polymer/material; lifecycle
weeks.quantitative: Half-life modeling and material lifecycle data.

weeks.title: Materials Science & Sustainable Chemistry Capstone
weeks.essentialQuestion: How can chemical principles guide a safer, more sustainable material or process?
weeks.phenomenon: A product must meet performance, cost, safety, and environmental constraints.
weeks.lab: Design/evaluate material or process using data; no synthesis of hazardous substances.
weeks.concepts: green chemistry; lifecycle; criterion; constraint; tradeoff; evidence
weeks.quantitative: Multi-criteria decision matrix and quantitative comparison.

weeks.title: Comprehensive Final & Laboratory Portfolio Defense
weeks.essentialQuestion: Can I integrate structure, reactions, energy, kinetics, equilibrium, and quantitative chemistry?
weeks.phenomenon: A multi-part industrial/environmental case requires several chemistry models.
weeks.lab: No new wet lab; cumulative final and portfolio defense.
weeks.concepts: cumulative synthesis
weeks.quantitative: Mixed stoichiometry, graphs, energy, equilibrium, data analysis.

assessment.unit: Performance task: model + data/quantitative reasoning + CER + application/design
assessment.midterm: 15-item cumulative objective check plus corrections and portfolio review
assessment.final: 30-item cumulative objective check plus portfolio/capstone defense

safety.lab_policy: Target ≥25% inquiry/laboratory time. Hazardous chemistry requires appropriately equipped, educator-supervised laboratory conditions; home learners use safe simulations/data alternatives.
safety.home_rule: Use only explicitly safe investigations; substitute simulation/data analysis whenever proper supervision or facilities are unavailable.
